name: Foliot Furniture
old_description: We invest in safe, well-run facilities, fair pay, and ongoing skills development across our 630+ person workforce. Since 2019, we have reduced recordable workplace injuries by nearly 80%. Our team benefits from on-site training, wellness programs, a bistro, a gym, collective insurance, and continuous professional development opportunities.
about:
Foliot Furniture, headquartered in Las Vegas, Nevada, was founded in 1991 by Daniel Foliot, a former aspiring lawyer who left a woodworking venture to start his own company. The business began with a focus on furniture for daycares and primary schools before expanding into higher education and hospitality.

With a workforce of more than 630 employees, Foliot produces laminate casegoods, seating, and upholstery for high-use environments, delivering over 1.25 million rooms to date. In 2024, it deployed 17 collaborative robots across its production lines.

Foliot serves student housing, hospitality, community living, staff housing, government, and maritime sectors. Clients include Savannah College of Art and Design, Cornell University, La Maison des Parents d'Enfants Handicapés des Laurentides, Spacesaver Interiors, and Ovation. The firm emphasizes vertical integration to control quality and lead times, with manufacturing in both the United States and Canada.

Foliot differentiates itself through vertically integrated manufacturing, warranties, and lifecycle support programs. The company cites its in-house design-to-delivery process, binational footprint, and commitment to safety—recordable injuries have fallen nearly 80% since 2019—as key advantages. A 2020 investment from Novacap supports continued expansion.

about:
Food Processing Equipment Company, LLC operates from Kalamazoo, Michigan. The company’s founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed. It began as a specialist in the used food processing machinery market, though the exact origins are not detailed on its website.

The firm buys, sells, and rebuilds used equipment for fresh vegetable, fruit, refrigeration, ice, freezing, cannery, and packaging lines. Its inventory includes individual machines such as conveyors, peelers, shredders, optical sorters, and drying systems, as well as complete processing plants. In addition to equipment sales, the company provides brokerage, auction, and investment recovery services, along with appraisals, line layout, installation, equipment financing, leasing, and consultation. It also supplies new Urschel blades for mechanical cutting machines.

The customer base spans food processors worldwide, ranging from small operations needing a single machine to large facilities requiring entire production lines. The company serves sectors including fresh and frozen produce, canned goods, and packaged foods.

The company positions itself as a one-stop source for both used and new machinery, emphasizing its ability to deliver complete plants or individual components and its focus on rebuilding equipment to manufacturer specifications.

name: Forever Fabrication & Welding Services
old_description: Forever Fabrication specializes in custom automotive fabrication for performance vehicles and automotive enthusiasts. Typical work includes custom exhaust systems, turbocharger piping, mounting brackets, and other performance upgrades.
about:
Forever Fabrication & Welding Services is based in Lake Elmo, Minnesota. The company was founded in 2017 by Matthew Belz, who began welding professionally in 2014 while attending Hennepin Technical College. After gaining experience in motorsports fabrication, stainless and aluminum TIG welding, and production manufacturing, Belz started the business as a side venture creating metal art and custom automotive components. A collaboration on a catalytic converter protection system during a nationwide theft surge helped the business grow and reach customers nationwide.

The shop provides precision TIG and MIG welding on stainless steel, aluminum, and mild steel, handling brackets, assemblies, fixtures, and subassemblies from drawings, sketches, or existing parts. It also offers fabrication development with CAD layout and precise measurement, and coordinates laser cutting, CNC machining, bending, and powder coating as needed. Forever Fabrication specializes in small- to medium-batch runs and short-run production parts. In addition to contract fabrication, the company designs and manufactures its own performance exhaust components—including universal equalizer tubes, Helmholtz-style resonators, and turbo manifolds for the GM Vortec 4200 inline-six—developed through real-world testing.

The business serves two main customer groups. For B2B clients, it supports machine shops, product development firms, equipment manufacturers, and fabrication companies that need overflow capacity or specialized TIG welding. For automotive enthusiasts, it builds custom exhaust systems, turbocharger piping, mounting brackets, and other performance upgrades, primarily through referrals in the local performance community. A noted reference is B&H Machine Co., Inc., which has used the shop for multi-year fabrication and welding projects.

Founder Matthew Belz emphasizes strong customer relationships, clear communication, and dependable manufacturing support. The company positions itself as a streamlined, single-source solution with consistent quality, fast turnaround, and responsive service, combining technical welding expertise with practical problem solving.

old_description: The Lancer family of modern design tables boasts a sculptural, majestic and unparalleled style. What makes Lancer a unique and precious model is the base with a strong architectural value, enlivened by a punchy graphic sign. Four blades cut through the air and intersect each other, creating an energetic composition with an apparently irreproducible pattern. Each leg is designed with a T-section, which multiplies the opportunities for crossing and overlapping.
about:
Format Furniture operates a high-end furnishings showroom in the SOHO neighborhood of Manhattan, New York. The company was established more than two decades ago by Brazilian designer Sany Marques, who carved a niche in the luxury furniture market by curating collections from international brands. Marques remains the owner, and showroom manager Robin Kay oversees daily operations.

Rather than manufacturing furniture, Format curates and sells modern and contemporary pieces from European lines such as Cattelan Italia and Arketipo Firenze. The showroom presents a continuous design philosophy centered on muted colors, non-patterned fabrics, and clean lines. A team of designers and sales consultants works with clients to specify furnishings for entire homes or commercial spaces, offering interior design consultation alongside product selection.

The clientele spans elite residential and commercial sectors. Format has furnished star-studded restaurants in New York and Las Vegas, kitchens and bathrooms for exclusive residential apartment buildings, and custom closets for hotels. The firm positions itself as a one-stop resource for complete project outfitting.

The company emphasizes a personalized experience—espresso or wine service, relaxed viewing, and dedicated design specialists—even as it handles large-volume projects. Marques’ predilection for a cohesive aesthetic gives the showroom a unified look that serves as a springboard for client ideas.

Four-In-One Inc. operates from its headquarters in Chelmsford, Massachusetts, with a second manufacturing facility in San Jose, California. The company, which does business as FOURINONE Inc/LLC, has built a reputation as a manufacturer of single-serving food products for the wholesale market.

Its product line includes homemade sauces, salad dressings, ketchup, jams, jellies, and condiments, all packaged in convenient single-serving sizes. Production takes place across two plants where quality assurance is integrated into manufacturing and packaging processes, supported by state-of-the-art production and packaging machinery and ongoing personnel training.

Four-In-One serves only the wholesale industry, working through a network of institutional food brokers and a distribution system the company describes as among the most efficient in the industry. It does not sell to private consumers, focusing instead on pallet and truckload shipments to wholesale customers.

The company emphasizes its reliable sales and distribution network, efficient delivery system that contributes to competitive pricing, and a commitment to using the finest ingredients. These factors, combined with continuous staff training and modern equipment, are presented as the foundation of its product quality and on-time delivery record.

The shop produces custom wooden furniture using traditional joinery techniques, emphasizing the natural integrity of each piece. Chad handles design, construction, and client consultation personally, working primarily with locally sourced wood when possible. The operation is scaled for one-off commissions and small batches, with no published facility size or employee count.

Chad founded the business to counter the trend of disposable, mass-produced furniture, aiming to build pieces that become cherished household fixtures. The differentiators he cites include traditional joinery, a collaborative design process, and a commitment to local materials.

name: G&G Industries
old_description: G&G Industries becomes the first manufacturer of Load Floors in North America using Polyurethane CSM Technology.
about:
G&G Industries was established in 1992 in Shelby Township, Michigan. The company began as a fabric die cutter and converter before expanding into automotive interior components.

The company specializes in honeycomb composite spray molding (CSM) for automotive interior trim and NVH components, including load floors, sunshade assemblies, and compression-molded parts. Operating from a 70,000-square-foot facility, G&G produces more than 1.3 million composite panels annually and supports production programs ranging from 10,000 to 500,000 units.

G&G serves automotive OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers, with its parts found in vehicles from Subaru, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, General Motors, Lexus, Toyota, Stellantis (FCA), Ford, Nissan, and Honda.

G&G was the first in North America to introduce honeycomb composite spray molding to the automotive industry in 2004 and the first to produce load floors using polyurethane CSM technology in 2007. The company emphasizes quality-driven processes, program management, and on-time delivery as core differentiators.
